banana noun

modern

Traupman 70
M-O

banāna, banānae f.

noun, first declension

An established modern borrowing recorded by both modern references. The long ā follows Morgan–Owens’s marked forms.

Other words

  • ariēna, ariēnae f.

    noun, first declension · also used · modern · Traupman 70; Pliny, N.H. 12.24: arborī nōmen palae, pōmō arienae

    Traupman 70, alongside banāna; from Pliny’s Indian fruit. No modern fruit sense is presented as Classical.

  • mūsa, mūsae f.

    noun, first declension · also used · medieval · M-O s.v. banana

    Medieval, and Linnaeus’s genus name Musa.

Examples

  • Banānam dēcorticēmus.

    Let’s peel the banana.composed

See also kiwi, avocado.

SourcesMorgan–Owens, Adumbratio: numbered food and kitchen sections

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 70–73.
